entity_title: Work permit applied for by employer
fact_text: In Bahrain the work permit for a foreign professional is applied for by the employer through the Labour Market Regulatory Authority (LMRA); it is issued against the employer's commercial registration, not obtained by the individual.
evidence_quote: employers can submit a request for issuing a new work permit for expatriate employees to be hired on their commercial registrations

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed the employee applies for their own Bahrain work visa. Actually the employer files the LMRA work-permit request on its own commercial registration (CR). Action: line up your Bahrain employer/CR before any permit step - you cannot self-file.

fact_text: The employer must bear all costs of employing, issuing and renewing the work permit and the worker's residency, and may not charge the worker any fee for issuing or renewing the work permit.
evidence_quote: without charging the worker any fees for the issuance or renewal of the work permit

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed the employee pays for their own work/residence permit. Actually LMRA rules make the employer bear all permit and residency costs and bar charging the worker. Action: do not accept salary deductions or invoices for permit/renewal fees - they are prohibited.

entity_title: Permit tied to the sponsoring employer
fact_text: The work permit is tied to the sponsoring employer: the expatriate employee may not work for any employer other than the one authorised in the permit.
evidence_quote: Not work for another employer other than the one authorized in the permit

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed a Bahrain work visa lets you work for anyone. Actually the permit authorises one specific employer only. Action: any second job or side work needs its own LMRA authorisation or a formal transfer first.

entity_title: Absence over 15 days breaches the permit
fact_text: An expatriate employee must not leave work (be absent) without lawful cause or the employer's permission for a period exceeding fifteen continuous days, or the permit conditions are breached.
evidence_quote: Not leave the work (Absence from work) without lawful cause or without the employer's permission or approval for a period exceeding fifteen continuous days

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed you can simply stop attending while sorting out a job change. Actually absence beyond 15 continuous days without cause/permission breaches the permit and can trigger an absconding report. Action: never let a gap exceed 15 days - get written leave or complete a transfer first.

entity_title: Flexi permit: work without a sponsor
fact_text: The Flexi Permit lets an eligible expatriate live in Bahrain and work in any non-specialised occupation without an employer-sponsor for a renewable one- or two-year period - a self-sponsored exception to the normal sponsored work permit.
evidence_quote: A permit allowing you to live freely in the Kingdom of Bahrain and work in any non-specialized occupation without a sponsor for a renewable period of one or two years

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed every worker in Bahrain needs an employer-sponsor. Actually LMRA's Flexi Permit allows sponsor-free work for eligible expats. Action: an employer-relocated professional normally uses the sponsored permit - treat Flexi as a fallback, not the default route (see eligibility limits).

entity_title: Employer must register address within 30 days
fact_text: The employer must give the Authority the worker's correct residential address; if none was given at application, it must be provided within 30 days of the worker's arrival in Bahrain, or the establishment's transactions are suspended.
evidence_quote: inform the Authority of the worker's correct address within 30 days from the worker's arrival in Bahrain

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed your Bahrain address is just personal admin. Actually LMRA requires the employer to register your correct address within 30 days of arrival or the whole establishment's LMRA transactions are frozen. Action: give HR your confirmed address fast - it can block colleagues' permits too.

entity_title: Biometrics required within one month of entry
fact_text: On first entry to Bahrain the expatriate employee must provide the Authority with fingerprints, a photo and a signature within a period not exceeding one month - the biometric registration underlying the CPR/ID.
evidence_quote: Provide the Authority with fingerprints, a photo, and a signature upon first entry into the Kingdom, within a period not exceeding one month

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed ID formalities can wait until you settle in. Actually biometrics (fingerprints, photo, signature) are mandatory within one month of first entry. Action: book the LMRA/NPRA biometrics appointment in your first weeks, not after.

entity_title: Pre-permit medical at a Wafid-accredited centre
fact_text: For an applicant outside Bahrain the work permit requires a medical examination issued by a health centre accredited by the Gulf Health Council (Wafid) in the home/residence country; the result must be a positive (healthy fit) report.
evidence_quote: the medical report must be issued by one of the accredited health centres by the Gulf Health Council (Wafid)

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed the medical check happens after arrival in Bahrain. Actually applicants abroad must pass a Wafid (GCC-accredited) medical in their home country before the permit issues. Action: use only a Wafid-listed centre; a report from a non-accredited clinic will not be accepted.

fact_text: If the expatriate employee fails the required medical examination, the employer must process the employee's deportation immediately - a failed medical blocks the residence/work permit.
evidence_quote: The employer must process the deportation of the expatriate employee immediately, if the employee had failed to pass the required medical examination

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed a minor health issue is negotiable. Actually a failed statutory medical obliges the employer to process immediate deportation. Action: resolve any known condition and confirm fitness before relocating dependants or shipping goods.

entity_title: Dependant residency covers children up to 24
fact_text: Dependant residence permits are requested by the employer for the employee's family; for children the dependant residency covers children up to the age of 24.
evidence_quote: employers can request the issuance of residence permits for their employees' dependants (children up to the age of 24)

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed dependent children lose residency eligibility at 18. Actually Bahrain's dependant residence permit covers children up to age 24. Action: adult children under 24 can still be sponsored - plan family residency around the 24 cutoff.

entity_title: Sponsoring dependants needs BHD 400 net income
fact_text: To sponsor dependants' residence permits the expatriate employee's monthly net income (as recorded at the Social Insurance Organization) must be BHD 400 or more.
evidence_quote: The expatriate employee's monthly net income (as per the Social Insurance Organization (SIO)) must be BHD 400 or more

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed any employed professional can bring family. Actually family sponsorship is income-gated: net monthly income (per SIO records) must be at least BHD 400. Action: confirm your SIO-registered net salary clears BHD 400 before planning to relocate dependants.

entity_title: Expat end-of-service pre-funded monthly via SIO
fact_text: For non-Bahraini private-sector staff, end-of-service gratuity is now pre-funded through the Social Insurance Organization: the employer pays a monthly subscription of 4.2% of monthly wages for the first three years of service (8.4% thereafter).
evidence_quote: The employer is obligated to pay a monthly subscription equal to 4.2% of the employee’s monthly wages for each of the first three years of service

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed end-of-service is a lump sum the employer pays out of pocket at the end. Actually since 2024 it is pre-funded monthly to SIO (4.2% then 8.4% of wages) and paid by SIO at separation. Action: check your SIO account shows monthly EOSG contributions - that, not a promise, is your accrued benefit.
